title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 19
paragraphs: Amyntas, seeing this, kept quiet—though he felt anger—because he was very much afraid of the Persians. But Alexander, son of Amyntas, who was present and saw this, being young and without experience of misfortune, was not able to hold back any longer. In his impatience he said to Amyntas: “Father, give in to what your age demands, and go away to rest, and do not persist any longer in the drinking; but I will stay here and provide our guests with everything needed.” At this Amyntas, understanding that Alexander intended some act of violence, said: “My son, I think I understand your words, as the heat of anger moves you—that you want to send me away and then commit some deed of violence. Therefore I ask you not to use violence against these men, lest it be our ruin; endure to look on at what is being done. As for my departure, however, in that I will do as you say.”
